42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton` — the collapse.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton` — hence `relPicMk` is injective.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMulEquivCechPic` — the resulting isomorphism

47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_overDualNumber_left`,
48	  `AlgebraicGeometry.picFromBase_overDualNumber_eq_bot` — the two Wave-5 instances.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMap` — the compatibility square: the
50	  equivalence intertwines `relPicMap` with `CechPic.map`. This is what makes the reduction
51	  usable rather than merely true, since Wave 5 computes the *kernel* of the `ε`-restriction,
52	  not just the groups at its two ends.
53	
54	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5 Thm. 5.11 (arXiv:math/0504020).

68	/-! ## The collapse at a one-point test object -/
69	
70	/-- **`picFromBase` is trivial at a one-point test object.** Classes on `C ⊗ T` pulled back
71	from `T` form the range of `CechPic.map (snd C T).left`; when `T.left` has a subsingleton
72	underlying space its Čech Picard group is trivial
73	(`Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`), so that range is `⊥`.
74	
75	No hypothesis on `C` whatsoever, and no commutative algebra: the argument is that a
76	one-point space has no cover with a nontrivial overlap. -/
77	theorem picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
78	    [Subsingleton T.left] : picFromBase C T = ⊥ := by
79	  refine le_antisymm (fun L hL => ?_) bot_le
80	  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff (C := C)).mp hL
81	  rw [← hN, Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton _ N, map_one]
82	  exact Subgroup.mem_bot.mpr rfl
83	
84	/-- **The projection to the relative Picard group is injective at a one-point test
85	object** — immediate from `picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton`, since a quotient by the
86	trivial subgroup separates points. Together with the landed `relPicMk_surjective` this makes
87	`relPicMk` bijective. -/
88	theorem relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	    [Subsingleton T.left] : Function.Injective (relPicMk C T) := by
90	  intro x y hxy
91	  have h := (QuotientGroup.eq (s := picFromBase C T)).mp hxy
92	  rw [picFromBase_eq_bot_of_subsingleton C T, Subgroup.mem_bot, inv_mul_eq_one] at h
93	  exact h
94	
95	/-- **`relPic C T ≃* Pic(C ⊗ T)` at a one-point test object.** The relative Picard group is
96	the *absolute* Čech Picard group of `C ⊗ T` there, because the subgroup being quotiented out
97	is trivial. This is what lets the Wave-5 ε-kernel computation be phrased on `CechPic`
98	directly, with no coset bookkeeping. -/
99	noncomputable def relPicMulEquivCechPic (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [Subsingleton T.left] :
100	    relPic C T ≃* (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic :=
101	  (MulEquiv.ofBijective (relPicMk C T)
102	    ⟨relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C T, relPicMk_surjective C T⟩).symm
103	
104	@[simp]
105	theorem relPicMulEquivCechPic_relPicMk (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [Subsingleton T.left]
106	    (L : (C ⊗ T).left.CechPic) :
107	    relPicMulEquivCechPic C T (relPicMk C T L) = L :=
108	  (MulEquiv.ofBijective (relPicMk C T)
109	    ⟨relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C T, relPicMk_surjective C T⟩).symm_apply_apply L
110	
111	/-! ## The two Wave-5 instances: `Spec k[ε]` and `Spec k` -/
112	
113	/-- The dual-number test object has a one-point underlying space: `Spec` of a local ring
114	whose maximal ideal is nilpotent. -/

168	    (t : (overSpec k A).left)

170	      (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
171	      (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L)
172	      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower k A L)
173	      (_ : IsScalarTower A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L),
174	      IsChartDatumPlusFibreAt C π μ D t L)
175	    (h : IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)) :
176	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
177	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLk, hLK, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hW, hW1⟩ := h
178	  obtain ⟨hAL, hAtow, hATow⟩ := towerOfResidueFieldExtension (k := k) t L
179	  have hid : PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
180	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
181	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
182	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass)) := by
183	    rw [← hM]
184	    exact hplus L hLf hLk hLK hLtow hAL hAtow hATow
185	  have hMcl : M = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A L) D.cechPicClass :=
186	    relPicMk_injective_of_subsingleton C (overSpec k L)
187	      (PicEtAff.unit_injective C L hid)
188	  refine (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
189	    (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) L).mpr ⟨W, ?_, hW1⟩
190	  rw [hW, hMcl]

192	/-! ## CHART-U(b)'s residue from `hfib` alone -/
193	
194	variable (C π) in
195	/-- **`IsChartDatumPresentation` FROM `hfib` ALONE** — no `hplus` side condition.
196	
197	`isChartDatumPresentation_of_plusFibre` asks for `hfib` *and* the per-point identity at every
198	extension.  The transport above supplies the second from the first, and
199	`towerOfResidueFieldExtension` supplies the tower instance the transport needs, so the caller
200	owes only `hfib`.
201	
202	**What this settles about the CHART-U(b) row.**  The row's state as of 2026-07-29 was "both
203	halves of the pointwise presentation are witness-free, and what remains is a `cechPicClass`
204	base-change identity at every extension of `κ(t)`, strictly more than `IsChartDatumPlusFibre`

207	along `PicEtAff.map`.  `isChartDatumPlusFibreAt_self` measured the gap from below (at
208	`L := κ(t)` the two coincide by `Iff.rfl`); this measures it from above, and the two together say

16	/-!
17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
18	
19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
23	
24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
29	
30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
36	-/

39	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

44	  CartesianMonoidalCategory

48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

50	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
54	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
55	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
56	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
57	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
58	
59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
60	
61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
69	  represents :
70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
72	  datum_class :
73	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
75	  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
76	  module_iso :
77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
80	  native_pushforward_base_change :
81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
82	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
83	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
84	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
85	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
86	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
87	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
88	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
89	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)

91	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
92	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

99	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) (U : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens) :
100	    Module P.cover.Carrier Γ(P.module, U) :=
101	  Scheme.moduleKSections
102	    (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module U

104	/-- The canonical `H^0` base-change equivalence attached to a rank-one presentation.
105	
106	This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
107	noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
108	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
109	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
110	    B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] (Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B]
111	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
112	  P.datum.datumH0BaseChange B
113	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing)

117	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
118	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
119	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward

128

131	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
132	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
133	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
134	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
135	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'

151	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅

188	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
189	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')

194	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app

196	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map P.evaluation := by

202	            (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)) ≫

214	the coefficient ring `B` and `relCurveMap` explicit while retaining the canonical cartesian

217	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)

232	    (snd C (overSpec k B)).left

/-!
# Finite subsets in affine opens

`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.

The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
the representability datum.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory
open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1

/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    FiniteInAffine X :=
  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩

/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
  intro s hs
  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
  intro y hy
  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩

/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
  intro s hs
  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩

11	
12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, a family of opens `U : J → X.Opens` and **transition
13	multipliers** `g i j ∈ Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ`, the glued sheaf of `informal/spec-dat-1.md`

17	(`AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSheaf`), together with

20	  `g i j · g j l = g i l` on triple overlaps) — a `Prop`-structure: the carrier needs no
21	  law (the matching relation is restriction-stable for arbitrary multipliers), the
22	  trivializations consume it;

24	  `j`-th component (`AlgebraicGeometry.gluedTriv`), commuting with restriction
25	  (`gluedTriv_res`), with the cross-piece comparison `gluedTriv_eq_unit_mul`
26	  (`triv_i = g i j · triv_j` on opens below both pieces — the m-chart mirror of
27	  `twistTriv₀_inf_eq`).

30	(DAT-1 stage 1b) is in `AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafQcoh`.
31	
32	## Implementation notes
33	
34	Sections are a genuine `Submodule` of the product of section modules (no defect map: the
35	m-chart defect target would be a product-of-products); every element computation is
36	`Scheme.resHom` bookkeeping, and restriction-path independence is definitional by proof
37	irrelevance of `≤` after `Scheme.resHom_resHom` collapse. The sheaf condition glues each
38	component in the structure sheaf of `k`-modules over the covers `{Wₐ ⊓ U j}ₐ` and checks
39	the matching relation locally, mirroring `isSheaf_twistPresheaf`. The `k`-module
40	structure on section modules is `Scheme.overModule`, activated locally per the house

10	/-!
11	# Cohomologous cocycles glue isomorphic sheaves (DAT-3, the `congrCoeff` transport)
12	
13	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, pieces `U : J → X.Opens` and two multiplier families
14	`g, g'` on the pairwise overlaps, a unit `0`-cochain `c : ∀ j, Γ(X, U j)ˣ` with
15	`c_i · g_{ij} = g'_{ij} · c_j` on every double overlap (the landed `IsCohomologous`
16	convention of the Čech Picard lane, in `resHom` spelling —
17	`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsGluingCoboundary`) induces an isomorphism of the glued
18	sheaves, componentwise `s_j ↦ c_j · s_j`:
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedCongrEquiv` — the `k`-linear equivalence of glued sections
21	  over every open `W`;
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.gluedSheafCongr` — the isomorphism of sheaves of `k`-modules
23	  `gluedSheaf k U g ≅ gluedSheaf k U g'`;
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_hModule_gluedSheaf_congr` — transport of cohomology
25	  vanishing across the isomorphism (via `Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv`).
26	
27	This is the m-chart generalization of the landed two-cover `congrCoeff` pattern
28	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule'.congrCoeff`, `Cohomology/RelativeTwoCover.lean`),
29	per the frozen W6-full spec (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §3.1(c)): cohomologous
30	cocycles present isomorphic glued sheaves. Neither multiplier family needs the cocycle
31	law — the transport is pure matching algebra.

43	`g` through the unit `0`-cochain `c`, i.e. `c_i · g_{ij} = g'_{ij} · c_j` in
44	`Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)` for all `i, j` (the landed `IsCohomologous` convention of the Čech
45	Picard lane, in `resHom` spelling). -/
46	def Scheme.IsGluingCoboundary {X : Scheme.{u}} {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens)
47	    (g g' : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ) (c : ∀ j : J, Γ(X, U j)ˣ) : Prop :=

60	`g` is cohomologous to `g'` through the inverse cochain `c⁻¹`. -/

62	    Scheme.IsGluingCoboundary U g' g (fun j => (c j)⁻¹) := by
63	  intro i j
64	  set a := X.resHom (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i) (c i : Γ(X, U i)) with ha
65	  set a' := X.resHom (inf_le_left : U i ⊓ U j ≤ U i)

71	  have hbb : b * b' = 1 := by rw [hb, hb', ← map_mul, Units.mul_inv, map_one]
